- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 3–5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d forecast); anchor to recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture volatility; add 1–2% volatility buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.7.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model underreacts; increase downward slope by 0.5–1% per day to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
